procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Winter visit. Slow season at work, short hours until March. Drinking more with the time off - AUDIT-C 12. Mood "bored, a little down," PHQ-9 7, no thoughts of self-harm. Eating less.
No bleeding since the fall. No falls.
Exam: AF 80s. Lungs clear. Abd soft. No edema. No asterixis.
A/P
- AUD: worse with the slow season. Long talk; he and partner are worried. Offered a structured plan to cut down safely given his seizure history - he wants to wait until he's back at work.
- Mood: mild symptoms in setting of slow season and drinking; recheck spring.
- AF/warfarin: INR in range.
- HFrEF, CLL, cirrhosis: stable labs.
- FIT kit.
RTC 3 mo.

documents.title: INR High
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR above range. No bleeding, no new meds. Drinking heavily, eating little. Hold 1 dose then resume 5 mg. Recheck 2 wks. FIT negative - told him.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Pulmonary
documents.author: pulmonary
documents.body:
Admit 03/29/2025 - discharge 04/02/2025
Diagnosis: right lower lobe aspiration pneumonia.

57-year-old man with severe alcohol use disorder, cirrhosis, recurrent aspiration pneumonias and an aspiration lung abscess in April 2024. His partner brought him in: four days of worsening cough and fever, after she found him unresponsive at home at the end of a three-day binge. Over the past few weeks, repeated vomiting and very little eating. Now coughing up brown, foul-smelling sputum, with right-sided chest discomfort.
T 38.5 C, pulse 106, BP 104/68, SpO2 91% on room air. Diminished breath sounds and coarse crackles at the right posterior base. CXR: RLL consolidation, no cavity.

Course: supplemental oxygen briefly; IV ampicillin-sulbactam, then oral amoxicillin-clavulanate. Afebrile by day 3. Withdrawal protocol without seizure. INR managed with warfarin continued.

Discharge meds: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 twice daily to complete 7 days; warfarin 5 mg, metoprolol succinate 25 mg, furosemide 20 mg, thiamine, folic acid, pyridoxine.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP in 1 week with INR; repeat chest x-ray in 6 weeks.

documents.title: Partner Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Partner called to let us know he was admitted Saturday with pneumonia. Improving per team. Will book hospital follow-up once discharged.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Admitted 3/29-4/2 with RLL aspiration pneumonia. Partner found him unresponsive after a 3-day binge; cough and fevers followed. Finished antibiotics yesterday. Coughing less, no fever, appetite coming back. Partner came with him today.
Exam: lungs: few crackles R base. AF 80s. Lost about 1.5 kg.
A/P
1. Aspiration pneumonia: improving. CXR in ~6 wks.
2. AUD: being found unresponsive is a new level. Talked with both of them. He says he is going to cut down when work restarts. Safety plan: don't stop abruptly, call us.
3. AF/warfarin: INR in range. With falls/unresponsive episodes, bleeding risk keeps climbing - will raise again with cardiology in July.
RTC 6 wks.

reports.text: PA and lateral. Comparison 03/29/2025. Right lower lobe consolidation has cleared. Small linear scar at the right base, unchanged. Heart enlarged, stable. No effusion.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt on his lunch break in his truck. Back at work full time since mid-April. No cough, no fever. CXR 5/13 clear apart from the old scar.
Drinking: says weekdays are "a few" and weekends still heavy.
A/P: aspiration pneumonia resolved. Continue current meds. In-person visit in August with INR before.

documents.title: Hematology Follow-up
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Hematology/oncology clinic, visit 06/05/2025
CLL, observation since 2021; s/p splenectomy; alcohol-related sideroblastic anemia.
Interval: aspiration pneumonia in March, recovered. No night sweats or unexplained fevers. No adenopathy.
CBC stable for him; Hgb around 13.
Assessment: CLL stable, no treatment indication.
Plan: return 1 year. Continue pyridoxine and folic acid. Asplenia precautions reviewed.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group, visit 07/10/2025
AF on warfarin; HFrEF EF 30%.
Interval: aspiration pneumonia admission in March after being found unresponsive. No heart failure symptoms beyond his baseline.
Meds: metoprolol succinate 25 mg, warfarin 5 mg, furosemide 20 mg.
BP 114/70, HR 78. No JVD. Lungs clear. Trace edema.
We discussed with him and his PCP's concern the balance of stroke prevention against bleeding with ongoing heavy alcohol use; his stroke risk score is low (1, for heart failure). He prefers to continue warfarin for now. Revisit if any further bleeding or falls.
Plan: no changes. Follow up 1 year.
Allergies: NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Summer check. Working long days. Mood better with work, PHQ-9 3. Drinking: weekday beers, weekend binges. No falls, no bleeding.
Cardiology in July: staying on warfarin for now, his choice after discussion.
Exam: AF 70s. Lungs clear. Abd soft. No edema.
A/P: stable on current regimen. INR in range. CMP at baseline. Flu/COVID in Oct. RTC Oct.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Fall visit. Feeling ok. No new symptoms. Breathing at baseline. Drinking unchanged. Slow season coming again in December - we talked ahead of time about the winter pattern.
Exam: AF controlled. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P
- AF/warfarin: INR in range.
- CLL/anemia: CBC stable.
- Cirrhosis: US due, ordered.
- HM: flu + COVID today.
RTC Jan.

reports.text:
Indication: cirrhosis surveillance. Comparison 11/21/2024.
Liver: coarse nodular liver, unchanged. No focal lesion. Portal vein patent, hepatopetal.
Gallbladder normal. No ductal dilation. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: No focal liver lesion. No ascites. Stable cirrhotic morphology.

documents.title: Anticoagulation Note
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. Continue 5 mg. US from November was stable - pt aware. Next INR with Jan visit.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Slow season at work again. Says he's keeping it to beer this year, no whiskey; partner nods but not convincingly. No falls, no bleeding, no blackouts since last spring.
Exam: AF 80. Lungs clear. Abd soft. No edema. No asterixis.

documents.author: RN

conditions.label: Fracture of right pubic rami, closed
conditions.note: Nondisplaced superior and inferior rami, nonoperative

medications.reason: Major hemorrhage; anticoagulation stopped at trauma discharge

medications.drug: acetaminophen 325 MG / oxycodone hydrochloride 5 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain, 7 days

reports.text: Focused assessment with sonography for trauma. Free fluid in the right upper quadrant and pelvis. No pericardial effusion.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Post-operative study. Recent laparotomy with midline incision; small amount of residual postoperative fluid, no active extravasation. Prior splenectomy. Nodular cirrhotic liver without laceration. Kidneys normal, no injury. Bowel without injury after repair. Pelvis: nondisplaced fractures of the right superior and inferior pubic rami. Sacroiliac joints and acetabula intact. Bladder normal.
reports.conclusion: Nondisplaced right superior and inferior pubic rami fractures. Post-laparotomy changes without active bleeding.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Trauma Surgery
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Regional trauma center
Admit 03/25/2026 - discharge 04/06/2026
Diagnoses: motor vehicle collision; hemorrhagic shock from mesenteric laceration; acute blood loss anemia; hypocalcemia after massive transfusion; nondisplaced right superior and inferior pubic rami fractures; multiple contusions.
Background: 58-year-old man with severe alcohol use disorder, cirrhosis, CLL, AF on chronic warfarin, HFrEF, prior splenectomy (atraumatic rupture) and Mallory-Weiss tear.

Arrival: hypotensive 90/60, HR 120. Alert but anxious. Multiple contusions, pelvic tenderness with suspected fracture, abdomen distended and tender. FAST positive. Warfarin reversed with prothrombin complex concentrate and vitamin K. Taken directly to the OR for exploratory laparotomy: actively bleeding mesenteric laceration, controlled and repaired; no bowel resection needed. Massive transfusion protocol. During the case he developed perioral numbness and carpopedal spasm. Post-transfusion: ionized calcium 0.9, Hgb 9, platelets 150, PT 16 s, PTT 40 s, lactate 3.2. IV calcium given with correction; lactate cleared.
CT after stabilization: nondisplaced right pubic rami fractures, managed nonoperatively, weight-bearing as tolerated with walker.
ICU 3 days, then ward. Alcohol withdrawal managed on protocol, no seizure. PT evaluation: home with walker and home PT.

Anticoagulation: warfarin stopped. Third major hemorrhage on warfarin; stroke risk score 1. Recommend he stay off; cardiology to confirm.
Discharge meds: oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 1 tab q6h prn x 7 days (acetaminophen total under 2 g/day); metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily; furosemide 20 mg daily; thiamine, folic acid, pyridoxine. STOP warfarin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP 1 week; orthopedic fracture clinic 2-3 weeks; trauma clinic for incision.

documents.title: Partner Call - Trauma Admission
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Partner called: car accident Wed evening, taken to the trauma center, surgery for internal bleeding, in ICU. Broken pelvis. She is overwhelmed; gave her our direct line. PCP aware. Warfarin INR checks on hold.

documents.title: Post-discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM call, day after discharge. Home with walker, partner with him. Pain controlled. Has his meds; warfarin was stopped by the trauma team, he understands not to restart. Hospital f/u booked 4/14. Discharge summary requested.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 8 days after discharge from the trauma center. MVC 3/25 - he does not want to talk about the details today. Bleeding mesenteric tear repaired at laparotomy, massive transfusion, low calcium during the case that was corrected. Right pubic rami fractures, no surgery. Warfarin stopped by trauma.
Now: walking with a walker, pain 4/10, using the oxycodone-acetaminophen once or twice a day, almost out and doesn't want more. Home PT twice a week. Incision healing. Partner home with him.
Alcohol: says none since the accident.
Exam: incision clean, staples out. Abd soft. Pelvis tender on R with movement. AF rate 80. No edema.
A/P
1. S/p trauma laparotomy, blood loss anemia: Hgb 10.7, recovering.
2. Hypocalcemia from transfusion: resolved, calcium normal today.
3. R pubic rami fractures: WBAT, walker, PT; ortho in 2 wks. Acetaminophen alone after the oxycodone runs out, max 2 g/day.
4. AF: off warfarin. Agree with stopping - third major bleed on it. Asked cardiology to weigh in.
5. AUD: sober 3 wks. Will support whatever he chooses; offered a counselor.
RTC 6 wks.

reports.text: AP pelvis with inlet and outlet views. Nondisplaced right superior and inferior pubic rami fractures with early callus. Alignment maintained. Sacroiliac joints and hips intact.
reports.conclusion: Healing nondisplaced right pubic rami fractures, alignment maintained.

documents.title: Orthopedic Fracture Clinic
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Orthopedic fracture clinic, visit 04/23/2026
Right superior and inferior pubic rami fractures, nondisplaced, after MVC 03/25/2026.
Walking with a walker, pain improving. X-rays: early callus, alignment maintained.
Plan: weight bearing as tolerated, advance from walker to cane with PT. Recheck in 10-12 weeks with x-rays.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group, visit 05/12/2026
AF; HFrEF EF 30%; alcoholic and tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy.
Interval: MVC 03/2026 with hemorrhagic shock and massive transfusion while on warfarin; warfarin stopped at discharge. This follows the 2023 splenic rupture (INR 3.5) and the 2024 Mallory-Weiss bleed.
No stroke or TIA symptoms. Walking with a cane.
Meds: metoprolol succinate 25 mg, furosemide 20 mg, vitamins.
BP 110/70, HR 80. Lungs clear. No edema.
Assessment: stroke risk score 1 (heart failure); three major bleeds on anticoagulation with ongoing alcohol use and cirrhosis. Risk of continuing clearly outweighs benefit.
Plan: remain off anticoagulation. Continue rate control. Follow up 1 year.
Allergies: NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two months out from the MVC. Off the walker, using a cane outside. Pain 2/10, acetaminophen a few times a week. PT finished last week. Hoping to go back to work in July, desk/supervisory only at first.
Cardiology 5/12: stay off anticoagulation. He's relieved.
Alcohol: started again in May, "a few beers at night," no liquor he says. AUDIT-C 8. Not interested in a program or medication; knows the offer stands.
No bleeding, no black stools.
Exam: walks with cane, mild antalgic gait. Incision healed. Abd soft, no ascites. AF rate 70s. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P
1. R pubic rami fractures: healing, ortho recheck in July.
2. Blood loss anemia after trauma: CBC today.
3. AF: off anticoagulation per cardiology; rate controlled on metoprolol.
4. HFrEF: euvolemic on furosemide 20.
5. Cirrhosis, CLL: CMP today. US due in Nov. Heme due June.
6. AUD: drinking again, lower than before by report. Counseled.
RTC 3 mo - front desk to call to book.

documents.title: Your labs from yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Piotr - your blood count is coming back up (hemoglobin 11.8). Liver and kidney numbers are at your usual. Nothing to change. Keep walking.

documents.author: pharmacy
documents.body: Refill request: metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily, 90 days. Approved per PCP protocol.

reports.text: AP pelvis. Right superior and inferior pubic rami fractures healed with bridging callus. Alignment anatomic. Hips intact.

Right pubic rami fractures, healed. Walking without a cane on level ground. X-rays: bridging callus.
Plan: full activity as tolerated; may return to work. Follow up as needed.
